title: Impact of SAF’s Overseas Training Detachments on Skills of Servicemen and Singapore's Defence Ties
what_it_is: Impact of SAF’s Overseas Training Detachments on Skills of Servicemen and Singapore's Defence Ties

sections.label: Overseas training space for SAF
sections.summary: Singapore's limited space constrains local SAF training, so overseas spaces like Shoalwater Bay allow realistic, complex training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: Singapore’s limited land, air and sea space constrains the scale and complexity of military training that the SAF can conduct locally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: With access to overseas training spaces, the SAF is able to hone its warfighting skills in complex scenarios, realistic conditions and varied terrain.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: For example, the Shoalwater Bay Training Area in Australia, which is the location for Exercise Wallaby, is about five times the size of Singapore.

sections.label: Benchmarking with foreign counterparts
sections.summary: Long-term overseas training detachments also let SAF learn and benchmark with foreign counterparts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: Long-term overseas training detachments also offer the added benefit of learning and benchmarking with our foreign counterparts.

sections.label: Community ties and flood relief
sections.summary: SAF personnel in overseas detachments join local community life, strengthening bilateral ties, and assisted Australia's flood relief.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: In addition to conducting regular exchanges with their professional counterparts, SAF personnel in our overseas training detachments participate actively in local community life and contribute back to the local communities, thus contributing to the strengthening of bilateral ties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: Our personnel also stand ready to render assistance in times of need, just as an example, our CH-47 Chinooks in Queensland had done so last month, in supporting Australia’s flood relief efforts.

sections.label: Safety culture and risk assessments
sections.summary: Safe training requires a strong safety culture and management system, with detailed risk assessments and injury-avoidance plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: Safe training can only be achieved with a strong safety culture and robust safety management system which emphasises both leadership accountability as well as personal responsibility of soldiers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: To achieve safety outcomes and zero fatalities in these exercises, detailed assessments of risks in each part of each exercise are required, together with concrete plans to avoid injuries.
